claims.text: Short-range chemical ordering is the primary governor of phase stability in near-equiatomic Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys.
Short-range chemical ordering governs retention of high-temperature strength.
Short-range chemical ordering governs retention of environmental resistance.
Short-range chemical ordering governs retention of radiation tolerance.
Short-range chemical ordering governs retention of cryogenic toughness.
Slow cooling after annealing promotes greater short-range chemical ordering than rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching produces a baseline with minimal short-range chemical ordering.
Enhanced short-range order locally lowers free energy.
Enhanced short-range order suppresses nucleation of deleterious secondary phases.
Enhanced short-range order suppresses growth of deleterious secondary phases.
Suppression of deleterious secondary phases stabilizes the phase structure.
The short-range-order-mediated microstructural modification improves high-temperature mechanical integrity.
The short-range-order-mediated microstructural modification improves environmental resistance.
The short-range-order-mediated microstructural modification improves radiation tolerance.
The short-range-order-mediated microstructural modification preserves cryogenic toughness.
Slow-cooled samples will have a more stable phase structure than rapidly quenched samples.
Slow-cooled samples will have superior high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness relative to rapidly quenched samples.
Under extreme thermal exposure or significant off-stoichiometry, factors other than short-range order may dominate phase stability.
